prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Linux and Windows operating systems.

learning_outcomes.text: The student can apply the basic concepts of virtualization in Linux namespaces and cgroups and build working basic virtual machines via KVM and Qemu.
The student masters the concepts of Qemu to execute code from CPUs with other ISAs on an x86 CPU (system emulation).
The student can set up and use an environment with Docker to create containers with persistent data volumes.

syllabus_topics: Lab assignments related to: Namespaces in Linux
Lab assignments related to: Container-based virtualization, Docker
Lab assignments related to: KVM, QEMU and libvirt

assessment_methods.method: Demonstration of design, elaboration and operation of realizations for lab assignments
Written reports on executing lab assignments

assessment_rules: The overall score is 50% from the written theory exam and 50% from the lab assignments. For the lab part, students are evaluated on demonstrating their realizations and submitting written reports. A demonstration is necessary to receive a score for each lab assignment. If a student scores less than 6/20 on one of the educational activities (theory or lab), the maximum overall score for the course unit will be 9/20. Resits for the written theory exam are possible; for the lab part, students can supplement or improve reports from the first exam period, otherwise, the first period's scores apply, with demonstrations still required.
